findings.F1: Fees take 0.000349 of the 0.000804 gross gain per coin per bar, about 43%, at a turnover of 0.33 of the book per bar; the 7100 trades last 1.8 days on average and lose 0.34% before fees and 0.44% after, so the book's mean daily return is 0.000446, below the 0.0005 bar and below holding's 0.00118.
findings.F2: The gain sits only in the largest scaled falls: on active bars where the coin fell over 60 days, the two lowest forecast quartiles have next-day excess returns of -0.00147 and -0.00080 and gross gains of -0.00001 and 0.00009, yet still pay fees of 0.00018 and 0.00029, while the top quartile earns an excess of +0.00623 (gross 0.00494); the 20-day split shows the same, -0.00087 and -0.00136 in the two lowest quartiles against +0.00504 in the top one.
findings.F3: The rebound appears only when volatility has expanded: in the lowest tercile of 20-day against 60-day volatility, active bars have excess returns of -0.00143 (t -1.19, n 1303) when the coin fell over 60 days and -0.00171 (t -0.74, n 603) when it rose, against +0.00518 (t 3.35, n 1088) and +0.00554 (t 2.87, n 818) in the highest tercile.
findings.F4: The book's deepest fall is -30.7% over 120 days, from w8 into w9, and w9 is its worst window at -0.0013 per day; the 30 worst book days average -8.0%, came with a prior position of 0.81 of the book, and followed a 20-day coin return of -16.8%.
findings.F5: Of the 0.000804 gross gain per bar, 0.000261 comes from the coins' own rise and the rest from timing, so cutting the bars that time badly (F2, F3) acts directly on the mean return, and on the fees that pull it below 0.0005.

ideas.idea: A coin's fall on a day, measured against its own volatility over the previous 20 days, is followed by a rise over the next 1 day, only while its 20-day volatility is high relative to its 60-day volatility; the larger the volatility-scaled fall and the higher that volatility ratio, the larger the next day's rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys the one-day rebound after sharp falls in a market whose volatility has just expanded, and stays out of rebounds in a calm market, where they lose and only pay fees.
ideas.name: rebound after volatility expansion

ideas.idea: A coin's fall on a day, measured against its own volatility over the previous 20 days, is followed by a rise over the next 1 day, with the rise growing faster than in proportion to the scaled fall, so that ordinary falls are followed by a weaker day than the coin's usual and only falls of several usual moves by a strong rebound.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys only after the deepest volatility-scaled falls, which removes most of the small trades whose fees exceed their gain.
ideas.name: rebound concentrated in extreme falls
